title: Fix variant skew when stickiness key is missing (use high-entropy fallback + Console warnings)
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes:
- Route experiments: missing stickiness keys no longer skew traffic to a single variant; requests without a stable key are evenly distributed using a per-request high-entropy fallback (non-sticky).
- Console: add warnings during experiment creation when stickiness keys/eligibility rules are likely to produce non-sticky assignments and noisy results.
description:
Context
We’ve seen skewed allocations in beta (most notably eu-west) when callers do not provide a stickiness key. The root cause was our “safe default” for bucketing: when the stickiness key source resolution produced an empty value, we were hashing a low-entropy sentinel (effectively a constant) which deterministically mapped the entire missing-key population to the same bucket → variant.

This PR fixes the data plane bucketing behavior to keep traffic splits correct even when stickiness is missing, and adds guardrails in Console so customers understand the tradeoff (even distribution but non-sticky assignment).

What changed
1) Policy engine / router bucketing
- Previous behavior:
  - stickiness_key = resolveStickyKey(req)  // may be "" / null
  - key_for_hash = stickiness_key ?? "unknown"
  - bucket = hash(experiment_id + route_id + key_for_hash)
  - Result: all missing-key requests share key_for_hash="unknown" → same bucket.
- New behavior:
  - If resolveStickyKey(req) yields a non-empty key: keep existing deterministic + sticky assignment.
  - If missing:
    - Use a high-entropy per-request fallback for bucketing only (req.request_id), explicitly marked as non-sticky.
    - Emit an internal annotation so we can debug / measure: assignment_key_source="request_id" and assignment_is_sticky=false.
    - Add a counter metric: route_experiments_missing_sticky_key_total{route_id, experiment_id}.

Rationale: Without a stable identifier we cannot be both sticky and well-distributed. For beta/GA safety we prioritize correct split distribution (avoids “variant 0 traffic” incidents) while making the non-sticky nature explicit in telemetry and UX.

2) Console warnings + validation hints
- Experiment creation wizard now surfaces a warning banner when:
  - stickiness_key is not explicitly set AND eligibility rules don’t guarantee a stable identifier (e.g., user_id / session_id header).
  - Copy: “Some requests may be assigned non-sticky using per-request bucketing. Metrics may be noisier; pass a stable stickiness key (recommended).”
- Console backend validation response includes a non-blocking warning code (EXPERIMENT_WARN_MISSING_STICKINESS_KEY) which the UI renders.
- Added an inline “Learn more” link to the troubleshooting section (kept behind the feature flag; docs PR will follow in redwood-docs).

3) Tests
- Unit tests for bucketing:
  - missing sticky key uses request_id and does not collapse to a constant key.
  - distribution sanity check: for a 50/50 split over N=20k synthetic requests with different request_ids, variant share stays within tolerance.
- Integration test updated to assert the response headers indicate assignment_is_sticky=false when the fallback is used.

Implementation notes
- We intentionally do NOT use IP / user-agent fingerprints for fallback due to privacy concerns and instability (proxy churn), and to keep cross-region behavior predictable.
- Request ID is already present in our request context plumbing and is high-entropy; it satisfies “even distribution” but not stickiness.
- Telemetry: the new metric is low-cardinality (route_id + experiment_id only) and should not materially impact costs.

Files / areas touched (high level)
- policy-engine: experiment evaluator / bucketing key selection
- gateway/router: plumb assignment metadata into request context (sticky vs non-sticky)
- console-api: validation warnings surfaced in create/update experiment endpoints
- console-web: wizard banner + copy updates
- tests: unit + e2e distribution sanity

Illustrative snippet (policy engine)
Old:
- key = stickyKey != "" ? stickyKey : "unknown"
- bucket = hash(experimentId + ":" + routeId + ":" + key)

New:
- if stickyKey != "":
    - keyForHash = stickyKey
    - sticky = true
  else:
    - keyForHash = requestId
    - sticky = false
- bucket = hash(experimentId + ":" + routeId + ":" + keyForHash)

Rollout / risk
- Behind existing route-experiments feature flag; applies only for experiment evaluation path.
- Risk: non-sticky assignment may surprise customers; mitigated via explicit Console warnings + new metric to quantify missing-key rate.
- SRE: alerts remain the same; this should reduce “variant receives ~0% traffic” situations caused by skew.

Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- Docs updates in redwood-docs to clarify stickiness key recommendations and how to verify via headers.
- Consider an optional “require sticky key” mode (hard validation) once we have more beta feedback.

Review notes / discussion (highlights)
- Allison Grant (Observability): Requested metric naming consistency + confirm low cardinality. Updated metric to route_experiments_missing_sticky_key_total and scoped tags to {route_id, experiment_id} only.
- Sean Gallagher (SRE): Asked for a clear operator signal to debug incidents. Added assignment_is_sticky annotation in debug endpoint output (internal) and ensured it’s present in logs when debug logging is enabled.
- Chloe Martin (Console backend): Requested non-blocking warning code to avoid breaking API clients. Implemented warning array in response; no change to success semantics.
- Dylan Brooks (Console & Tooling): Asked for UX copy to avoid implying statistical guarantees. Updated wording to “noisier results” and pointed to recommended best practice.

Checklist
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] E2E test updated for missing-key path
- [x] Metric added + reviewed for cardinality
- [x] Console warning behind feature flag
- [x] Linked to SUP-24831 (beta customer report)

CI
- Build: pass
- Lint: pass
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration tests: pass

Outcome
Merged (squash) into main. Will be included in the next beta patch rollout for route experiments.
commits: policy-engine: treat missing stickiness key as non-sticky + use request_id for bucketing
router: propagate assignment_is_sticky + assignment_key_source into request context
console-api: return EXPERIMENT_WARN_MISSING_STICKINESS_KEY during experiment validation
console-web: creation wizard warning banner + copy tweaks
tests: add distribution sanity test for missing-key population
review_conversation:
Allison Grant: Can we confirm this doesn’t introduce high-cardinality tags? route_id can already be high depending on normalization.
Jordan Lee: Good call. The new counter only tags {route_id, experiment_id} (no variant/model/region). Route_id is the normalized template form per the earlier decision, same as existing route-level metrics.

Sean Gallagher: Please add an explicit signal for oncall to differentiate ‘sticky’ vs ‘non-sticky’ assignments when debugging skew reports.
Jordan Lee: Added assignment_is_sticky + assignment_key_source into request context and ensured the internal assignment debug endpoint prints both fields.

Chloe Martin: For Console validation, can we avoid failing create/update? Beta customers already have automation that would break.
Jordan Lee: Agreed. Implemented warnings as non-blocking; API returns warnings[] and UI renders banner. No change to status codes.

Dylan Brooks: UX copy should avoid implying that missing stickiness invalidates results; it’s more about noise and interpretation.
Jordan Lee: Updated banner text to ‘may be noisier’ + recommends passing stable stickiness key; removed stronger language.
